content:
This week, Apple launched its next-generation M6 chip in the new Mac mini. But there are still several products that will soon be upgraded to M6. Here's the rumored M6 Mac and iPad release schedule.

Fall 2026: MacBook Pro and iMac

This fall, likely October, Apple is expected to launch two more M6 Macs:

  • MacBook Pro
  • iMac

The MacBook Pro will only be the 14-inch base model. According to Mark Gurman, Apple skipped the M6 Pro and Max versions. So only the entry-level MacBook Pro will upgrade to M6, and the next batch of Pro-tier chips won't arrive until the M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple's new iMac is not expected to change much beyond the M6 chip. The only other rumored upgrade is some new color options. But going from M4 to M6, the new model is still worth upgrading.

Worth noting is that the rumored MacBook Ultra is not on this list. It is expected to launch in the fall, but will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, not M6.

Spring 2027: iPad Pro and MacBook Air

The first batch of rumored 2027 products to upgrade to M6 includes:

  • iPad Pro
  • MacBook Air

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it upgraded to the M5 chip. With a rumored spring 2027 update, this product will follow its usual 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond the M6 chip upgrade, Apple's new iPad Pro is expected to add a vapor chamber cooling design. This would improve the sustained performance of this ultra-thin machine.

The MacBook Air with M6 chip is expected to launch around the same time as the iPad Pro. February through April is possible, but based on Apple's track record, March is the safest bet.

Beyond the chip upgrade, there are few other rumors about the new MacBook Air. It should continue the same design as the M5 model. And reports suggest an OLED upgrade won't come until at least 2028, so the display will likely remain unchanged.

One potential benefit of M6 for iPad Pro and MacBook Air is improved battery life. Apple says the 2-nanometer process used in M6 brings "major leaps in performance and energy efficiency".

Are you planning to upgrade to any of these new M6 products? Why? Let us know in the comments.
